sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into India (IndiGo's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering India, not a rule stated by IndiGo for its cabin. The Indian customs passenger guide allows alcoholic liquor, wine or beer up to 2 litres within the duty-free allowance for incoming passengers, next to 100 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 125 g of tobacco. Above the allowance, the guide gives the rate for all alcoholic beverages other than beer, including wine, as basic customs duty of 50% plus an agriculture infrastructure and development cess of 100%, and for beer basic duty of 100% plus a 10% social welfare surcharge. These rates come from a guide that may be out of date, so check the current rates with Indian customs before you carry more than the allowance. The guide gives no minimum age and no penalty for alcohol. Some Indian states also restrict alcohol themselves, which the guide does not cover. Source read: CBIC, Customs clearance of passengers at a glance (PDF). The rates may have changed since the guide was issued.

sources: IATA — Dangerous Goods Regulations, Table 2.3.A (67th edition, 1 January 2026)

sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into South Africa (South African Airways's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering South Africa, not a rule stated by South African Airways for its cabin. The South African Revenue Service guide on duty-free allowances for travellers says a traveller may import free of duty and tax 2 litres of wine and 1 litre of other alcoholic drinks, including beer, along with 200 cigarettes, 20 cigars, 250 g of tobacco, 250 ml of eau de toilette and 50 ml of perfume. The tobacco and alcohol allowances are not available to anyone under 18, and crew members are not entitled to any duty-free consumables. Consumables above the limits cannot be claimed under the duty-free allowance, and full duty and VAT must be paid on the excess. The allowance may be used once per person in a 30-day cycle after an absence of more than 48 hours. A flat rate allowance lets you bring additional goods up to R20,000 at 20%. The guide does not describe penalties for undeclared alcohol. Source read: SARS, SC-PA-01-03 Duty-free allowances for travellers (external guide, PDF). Penalties are not in the part read.

sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into Kenya (Kenya Airways's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering Kenya, not a rule stated by Kenya Airways for its cabin. The Kenya Revenue Authority says travellers may bring up to 1 litre of spirits or liquor and up to 2 litres of wine without declaring, and perfume up to half a litre in total, with no more than a quarter of that as perfume. Duty-free purchases above these amounts must be declared. Cigarettes, cigars and tobacco are allowed up to 250 grams combined. Passengers get a US$2,000 concession for personal or household goods, but alcohol, perfume and tobacco are not covered by it beyond the limits above. Goods bought abroad above US$500 must be declared. Failing to declare or misdeclaring goods breaches Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act and goods are liable to seizure or confiscation. Source read: KRA, Passenger terminal clearance in Kenya.

sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into Iceland (Icelandair's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering Iceland, not a rule stated by Icelandair for its cabin. Icelandic Customs (Skatturinn) counts the alcohol allowance in units. It names spirits as drinks above 21% alcohol and wine as any non-beer drink at 21% or below, and gives example combinations such as 1 litre of spirits plus 0.75 litre of wine plus 3 litres of beer, or 3 litres of wine and 6 litres of beer, or 1 litre of spirits and 6 litres of beer, or 1.5 litres of wine and 12 litres of beer, or 18 litres of beer. The minimum age for bringing alcohol into Iceland is 20 and for tobacco 18. The goods must be for personal use or gifts, not for sale, and travel agencies, guides or drivers cannot import duty-free goods on a traveller's behalf. Use the red channel if you have dutiable or restricted goods. The page does not state a penalty for exceeding the alcohol allowance. Source read: Skatturinn, Duty-free imports (English). No alcohol penalty is stated.

sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into Brazil (Azul's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering Brazil, not a rule stated by Azul for its cabin. The Brazilian Federal Revenue (Receita Federal) says a traveller may bring up to 12 litres of alcoholic drinks in total in baggage, by air, sea or land. Over the limit, the drinks are treated as ordinary baggage without the tax exemption. The arrival Free Shop has its own limit: at a land border up to 12 litres, and at a port or airport up to 24 units, with no more than 12 units of any one type of drink. Travellers under 18 cannot buy alcohol at the Free Shop, even when accompanied, and alcohol cannot be part of the baggage of a child or teenager even with a legal guardian. The page does not mention wine or beer separately, so the rules apply to alcoholic drinks in general. Purchases above the extra arrival quota are taxed under the special RTE regime, which the page does not explain, and it gives no fine for exceeding the limit. Source read: Receita Federal, Cota de isenção, duty free e bagagem tributável (in Portuguese). The RTE regime and fines are not explained on the page.

sections.h: What customs says about bringing alcohol into Singapore (Singapore Airlines's home country)
sections.p: This is the customs rule for people entering Singapore, not a rule stated by Singapore Airlines for its cabin. Singapore Customs says the liquor concession needs you to be 18 or older, to have spent at least 2 days abroad, not to arrive from Malaysia, and the liquor must be for personal use. The options are 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of wine, or 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of beer, or 1 litre of wine plus 1 litre of beer, or 2 litres of wine, or 2 litres of beer. Crew have their own smaller options, and there is no concession at all for travellers arriving from Malaysia. Liquor above the concession incurs duty and GST, and more than 10 litres needs a Customs permit. Failing to declare goods at the Red Channel may result in fines or prosecution. The S$500 GST relief for newly bought goods excludes liquor and tobacco, and tobacco has no concession at all. Source read: Singapore Customs, Duty-free concession and GST relief. Fine amounts are not on the page.

faq: How much perfume can I take in my Turkish Airlines cabin bag?
Turkish Airlines says a maximum of 100 ml is permitted in the cabin for hair sprays, perfumes, colognes and medicines containing alcohol.
Can I take duty-free liquids through a Turkish Airlines transfer?
Not always: at some airports transiting passengers cannot pass transit security with liquids over 100 ml, including sealed duty-free bags.

Pegasus says cosmetic products carried in the cabin cannot be more than 100 ml each, and too many liquid products may not be accepted.
Can I take baby food on Pegasus?
Yes, Pegasus says essential products such as baby food can be carried in zip bags in cabin baggage.

alcohol.answer: Pegasus publishes the passenger dangerous-goods table (document effective 1 January to 31 December 2023). It lists alcoholic drinks of more than 24% and up to 70% alcohol in retail packaging, in receptacles of up to 5 L and 5 L in total per person, and says drinks of 24% or less are not subject to any restrictions.

faq: How much strong alcohol can I take on Pegasus?
Pegasus's 2023 passenger dangerous-goods document allows drinks of more than 24% and up to 70% alcohol in retail packaging, in containers of up to 5 L and 5 L in total per person.
Is wine or beer restricted on Pegasus?
The same document says alcoholic beverages containing 24% or less alcohol by volume are not subject to any restrictions.
sources: Pegasus: Provisions for Dangerous Goods Carried by Passengers or Crew (document effective 2023)

perfume.answer: Pegasus's own passenger dangerous-goods document (effective 2023) covers perfumes, colognes and hair sprays: the total net quantity of such toiletry articles and non-flammable aerosols must not exceed 2 kg or 2 L, and each single article must not exceed 0.5 kg or 0.5 L.

sections.h: What Pegasus's own document says about perfume and aerosols

Security checkpoints can apply the separate 100 ml liquid limit in the cabin; this document does not address it.

faq: How much perfume can I take on a Pegasus flight?
Pegasus's 2023 dangerous-goods document sets 2 kg or 2 L in total for toiletry articles such as perfumes and hair sprays, and 0.5 kg or 0.5 L for each single article.
Do aerosol sprays need a cap on Pegasus?
Yes. The document says release valves on aerosols must be protected by a cap or other suitable means to prevent inadvertent release of the contents.
sources: Pegasus: Provisions for Dangerous Goods Carried by Passengers or Crew (document effective 2023)

Almost none: only cosmetics, toothpaste and shaving cream for use during the trip, under the page's conditions.

alcohol.answer: China Eastern allows drinks up to 24% alcohol without limit, and 5 litres per person of drinks from 24% to 70% in checked baggage; above 70% is prohibited. Alcohol must go in checked baggage, except what you buy in the passenger terminal, which may go on board.

Up to 24% alcohol has no limit; 24% to 70% is limited to 5 litres per passenger in checked baggage; above 70% is prohibited.
Can I carry alcohol in the cabin on China Eastern?
Only alcohol bought in the passenger terminal. Other alcohol must be checked.
Can I drink my own alcohol on China Eastern?
No. Passengers may drink only alcohol served on board by China Eastern.

On domestic flights liquids are banned except self-use cosmetics, toothpaste and shaving cream.

Does duty-free perfume change on a China Eastern connection?
If you transfer to a domestic flight in the secure zone, it needs proof of purchase and a sealed intact bag; if you leave the secure area it becomes checked baggage.
